messages:
jessica: heads-up — canary run for onnx-quant-llama2@v2 is showing a regression on the eval harness, PPL jump and degraded ranking metric :warning:
omar: which job? can you paste the CI link or job id?
jessica: job: eval-canary/onnx-quant-llama2/v2 #42, ran at 2039008600. Summary: 5 runs, median metric delta +3.9% on our pass/fail suite, failures all in reranking tests.
liam: logs? stack traces? could be kv-cache mismatch after the quant kernels landed
sasha: infra: runner-12 had an out-of-memory during the quant compile step but the actual eval tasks executed on runner-7 and runner-9 fine. no disk errors.
ci-bot: [eval-canary/onnx-quant-llama2/v2 #42] FAILED — 5/5 trials failed threshold. logs: https://ci.internal/r/42 :rotating_light:
omar: can someone run a quick bisect against the last few PRs to narrow cause? my hunch is the kernel fallback change from last week (PR 4519) interacting with quant path
jessica: i'm starting a local bisect now. steps:
```
git checkout canary-ref
git bisect start HEAD canary-base
# running harness script: ./scripts/run_eval_canary.sh --workdir /tmp/canary
```
liam: note: the harness uses tokenization mapping v3 since monday (PR 4524). tokenization mismatches often look like metric flips but are actually off-by-one tokens. check token counts in the failing traces.
jessica: good flag — initial logs show alignment differences. sample from failing trial:
```
INPUT: "Who is the president of X?"
TOKEN_IDS_EXPECTED: [112, 45, 78, 9]
TOKEN_IDS_ACTUAL:   [112, 45, 78]
```
omar: that does look like tokenization drop. but why only in quant? both float and quant should use same tokenizer. maybe a packaging change omitted the tokenizer artifact in the quant build.
sasha: I pulled the artifact list from the canary container: quant build missing tokenizer-v3.tar.gz. last good canary has it. I can attach via s3: s3://redwood-canaries/onnx/quant/2026-03-19/artifacts.json
ci-bot: artifact-checker: tokenizer-v3.tar.gz MISSING in build artifacts for onnx-quant-llama2@v2 :warning:
liam: aha. that would produce token ID truncation and the observed reranking drop. If tokenizer is missing, input pipeline may fall back to a legacy tokenizer with different special tokens.
jessica: decision proposal: hold the dedicated rollout and block the public release. revert the packaging change that omitted tokenizer artifact (PR 4538) and re-run canary. anyone object? :eyes:
omar: +1. also add a harness assertion to fail-fast when tokenizer artifact checksum is absent. we should not let this silently pass again.
sasha: creating rollback PR now — PR 4541 reverting 4538 and adding artifact-presence check in the build manifest. tagging oncall @sasha for deploy review. ETA ~25 minutes.
jessica: adding a quick CI patch to the eval runner to assert token counts equal expected at the start of each trial to avoid expensive full-run flakiness: `if len(tokens) != len(expected): raise HarnessConfigError('tokenizer mismatch')`
liam: after rollback we should re-run both quant and float canaries and run a small A/B on the metric suite. also run a quick end-to-end sample prompt set to validate alignment.
ci-bot: [PR 4541] opened by sasha — https://ci.internal/pull/4541 :white_check_mark:
omar: timeline: if rollback merges and canary passes we can resume rollout in next window. if it still fails, escalate to a kernel/quant interaction triage.
jessica: for postmortem, capture: packaging regression (tokenizer omitted) -> harness didn't assert artifact presence -> canary surfaced metric regression. action items: rollback (sasha), harness artifact check (omar), token-count assert (jessica), cross-check release pipeline to ensure artifacts listed in manifest (platform).
sasha: ack, will post PR link and canary re-run results here. thanks all :thumbsup:
